pre-visibility-flip leak scan; read-only denylist/term-matching over the tree

worktree wrapper, workspace-root-confined by construction; consumed by WorktreeCreate + dispatch
one-line ceremony-tier classification printed by /foundry:intake
read-only control-plane preflight probe run at /foundry:init
advisory context-diet lint over an assembled dispatch prompt; fail-open, flags-only

writes only six fixed filenames under the CONFIGURED usage.dataset; reads the collector dir the operator names; numeric fields only (configured `usage.dataset` only: an explicit `--dataset` is the ask row below)
derives attribution.jsonl under the CONFIGURED usage.dataset from usage + bindings; numeric fields only (configured `usage.dataset` only: an explicit `--dataset` is the ask row below)
read-only coverage report over the configured dataset
reads the operator's own transcript directory; writes usage rows under the configured dataset (configured `usage.dataset` only: an explicit `--dataset` is the ask row below)
appends an attribution record (session -> issue/operator) to <dataset>/bindings.jsonl; wrong bindings misattribute cost, so the write is not silent

`--dataset DIR` redirects ingest/bind/attribute writes to a caller-named directory instead of the configured usage.dataset; the explicit form is not silent (the configured-dataset form stays in the allow row)
read-only per-worker env-isolation check consumed by the env-reap hook
read-only intake schema-defect / grounding checker over a project dir
read-only per-repo status rows through the hardened choke point; no network, no mutation.
read-only manifest⟷reality⟷gitignore round-trip incl. the reverse scan; surfaces, never fixes.

Read-only registry-integrity report (feat-foundry-repo-registry-formalization): physical-confinement + gitignore-pairing + origin-match rows over .claude/foundry-project.json; single read-only git choke point, sanitizing emission sink, writes nothing. Tiered at merge-reconciliation when the script landed after the map (the closed-world tripwire firing as designed).
session-scoped mode/fork-policy set-and-resolve state-writer; not a release/repo ceremony
ceremony: front-authorization; --yes/--skip-audit-reason arrive after other args, not prefix-keyable, so the whole script is ask
writes GLOBAL git config (--global --unset-all/--get-regexp, two includeIf.*.path writes); machine-scope state
ER class-C release-cut ceremony marker, taken at the coarser fail-safe tier; the script itself mutates no tree
pinned ceremony (AC-PFM-3): documented no-op today, but the flag is the shape a future auto-heal would reuse
issues gh pr merge <pr> --squash once every check is green — a merge is a repo-state mutation, ask like foundry-authorize.py, never a self-grant

pinned ceremony (AC-PFM-3): re-writes the lock in place; leading flag verified prefix-keyable; the split tier with --validate/--load is safe ONLY because main() checks those flags before --relock — a combined invocation runs the earlier-checked verb (security review 2026-08-02).
read-only classification of every worktree/branch matching the discipline's naming glob; --apply below is the deletion tier (branch-and-worktree-discipline, AC-BWD-2)

deletes the merged class's worktrees + local (git branch -d, falling back to -D only on that refusal, narrated) AND remote branches (git worktree remove, git push origin --delete) -- a repo-state mutation, ask like foundry-merge-when-green.py's own merge call, never a self-grant
foreach fans an operator-supplied command over every present repo — arbitrary exec from the agent's hands prompts; the operator's own in-terminal use is unaffected.

sync clones/fetches from manifest-declared remotes — the factory's first network egress; the manifest write is the standing consent, the ask is the per-run operator moment (feat-foundry-workspace-repo-verbs). Subcommand split is reach-disjoint: argparse positional subcommands, first token decides the verb.

attach-existing writes the manifest + gitignore pairing and hands the new row to reconcile (clone/fetch egress) - a workspace mutation with network reach prompts per run; the preview is the consent surface (feat-foundry-wizard-attach-repo-flow).

create-new invokes `gh repo create` under the operator's identity then falls through to attach - remote resource creation always prompts. Subcommand split is reach-disjoint: argparse positional subcommands, first token decides the verb (feat-foundry-wizard-attach-repo-flow).
--apply POSTs repository rulesets with an Administration (write) token; it writes the merge floor itself

`cutover --apply` creates GitHub issues and writes .foundry/migration/** plus one appended migrated_to key per selected manifest; `cutover record` creates authority.yaml; inventory/preview are read-only. One rule for the script: the write verbs decide the tier (gn-14).

render writes governance/rendered/ and baseline writes governance/local/baselines/; load, validate, applicable, check and exceptions are read-only and run silently through the plugin-scripts-allow hook; no network
executes the command it is given under a host-sized flock slot, so it is never silent (gv-12)
renders the brief preamble to stdout from local governance files; writes nothing, no network

`emit` posts a structured comment on a GitHub issue under the operator's identity (a content-creating write); `parse` is read-only. One rule for the script: the write verb decides the tier (gn-04 deck events).
read-only discovery-coverage probe: REST GET, search and GraphQL `query` only, every call timeout-bounded; writes nothing to GitHub or the workspace (gn-03 capability check).

read-only leader-board report: gh issue list/view, REST GET and GraphQL `query` only, plus reads of the usage dataset; computes statistics to stdout and writes nothing to GitHub or the workspace (gn-15).

read-only inbox scan: GitHub search, notifications and issue views only; writes nothing to GitHub and only the gitignored runtime inbox.json in the workspace; never posts a comment (gn-09 operator inbox).
reads the persisted runtime inbox.json only; no network, no writes (gn-09).
posts an `ack` marker comment on a GitHub issue/PR under the operator's identity (gn-09).
posts a `scheduled`/`rescheduled` marker comment on a GitHub issue under the operator's identity (gn-09).
posts a `resolved` marker comment with evidence on a GitHub issue under the operator's identity (gn-09).

scan plus WRITES: posts `scheduled`/`blocker_ack` marker comments on GitHub issues under the operator's identity via the gn-04 writer; tiered ask like ack/schedule/resolve because its reach includes GitHub writes, which the read-only `scan` verb does not (gn-09). The `resolve` evidence rule is a practice, not a control.
absolute anti-pattern: unattended bulk local-state destruction
absolute anti-pattern: bypasses required reviews/checks on the merge floor
absolute anti-pattern: unattended destructive infra apply with no plan review
read-only: git log numstat + gh pr list over the window; prints one measured line per repo (paper:code, PRs, lead time); replaces status reports

adopts a GitHub issue as the active ticket: writes only the git-dir ticket file; refuses a Done-means command from an author without write access on the issue's repo unless --trust-author (which the plugin-scripts-allow hook never auto-allows — the session's own permission mode decides)
records a paper path on the active ticket (git-dir file only)
read-only
deletes the git-dir ticket file only

read-only: reads the operator's assigned issues from GitHub (gh api graphql/user, queries only) and prints the selection; writes nothing; skips (never selects) an issue whose Done-means is not author-trusted

read-only: reads one issue from GitHub (gh api graphql/user and the collaborator-permission probe, queries only) and prints the trust-checked view (done_trusted, done_digest, last_edited_by); executes nothing, writes nothing

POSTs a structured `start` comment on a GitHub issue under the operator's identity (a content-creating write) and writes the git-dir claim record; refuses unassigned / other-owned issues and the WIP limit; never self-assigns (gn-08); refuses (typed `done-means-untrusted`) an issue whose Done-means command is not author-trusted unless the operator passes --trust-author (never auto-allowed by the plugin-scripts-allow hook)

reads current GitHub issue state + timeline and reports stop_dispatch per started issue; no GitHub write. Its only local write is pruning claim records for issues GitHub reports closed from the git-dir claims file (a cache, never authority)
local file only: acquire/renew/release/check the lease at <workspace>/.foundry/runtime/lead.json; no network, no GitHub write
EXECUTES the ticket's Done-means command (input taken from an issue body): the session's permission flow decides, never a silent allow (security review of #270, R1)

EXECUTES the repository's own test command (Taskfile/Makefile/npm/pytest — code the branch defines): the session's permission flow decides; local-green is a delivery convenience, not a reason for a silent allow (security review of #270, R2)
